description: Classifies a self-conscious episode (did the agent, by its own knowledge, meet a Standard; what attribution locus applies; did any witness form a belief -- possibly diverging from ground truth -- that the standard was violated) into {hubristic_pride, authentic_pride, shame, guilt, embarrassment, none}, per the Lewis (1971) / Tracy & Robins (2004, 2007) / Miller (1996) / Tangney, Miller, Flicker & Barlow (1996) appraisal literature -- SELF_CONSCIOUS_EMOTIONS_PREREG.md. Reuses the SmEntity-belief_world nested-belief SHAPE domains/character_tom.py already established (a witness's belief about the agent is a node structurally distinct from ground truth), applied to a NEW, live-encounter trigger (WitnessBelief nodes minted mechanically, not via NLP attitude-sentence parsing) and NEW, reflexively self-directed content (a witness's judgment of the APPRAISING agent). standard_met drives the shame/guilt/pride axis regardless of exposure (Tangney et al. 1996); perceived_violation -- read from witness belief, which may diverge from standard_met -- drives embarrassment specifically, gated to the circumstance-attributed cell (Miller 1996). Zero new Rust Terms.

concepts.name: self_conscious_emotion_appraisal
concepts.definition: A self-conscious emotion (pride/shame/guilt/embarrassment) is a categorical function of standard-compliance, attribution locus (global-self / specific-act / circumstance), and perceived (not necessarily actual) social exposure -- distinct emotions for the same outcome depending on WHERE the cause is attributed, and one specific cell (circumstance) gated on whether any witness believes a violation occurred, independent of whether one actually did.
concepts.why: The user asked whether CAN/PSI can produce embarrassment 'and otherwise' -- a research pass found three missing primitives (reflexive second-order belief, a violable Standard, attribution-locus classification); this seed supplies all three. SELF_CONSCIOUS_EMOTIONS_PREREG.md.

rules.name: sc_decide_emotion
rules.comment: PREREG Sec2-3: classifies a self-conscious episode into {hubristic_pride, authentic_pride, shame, guilt, embarrassment, none} from (standard_met, attribution_locus, perceived_violation). standard_met (the agent's OWN ground truth) drives the shame/guilt/pride axis regardless of exposure (Tangney, Miller, Flicker & Barlow 1996: shame/guilt are NOT reliably audience-dependent). perceived_violation -- Exists over WitnessBelief.judgment, which may DIVERGE from standard_met -- drives embarrassment specifically, gated to the circumstance-attributed cell only (Miller 1996: embarrassment attributes to circumstance/involuntary exposure, not a moral standard violation; Tangney et al. 1996: embarrassment IS reliably audience-dependent, the one cell this design gates on exposure). Pride bifurcates the same way shame/guilt do (Tracy & Robins 2007): global_self attribution -> hubristic, specific_act attribution -> authentic. attribution_locus is CATEGORICAL (Lewis 1971's three-way split), not a continuous scalar, so this is a genuine lookup table (IfThenElse), not a misapplied Argmin-over-codebook quantization. Zero new Rust -- Eq/And/IfThenElse/Let/Exists/Neighbours/Attr/Var/Lit all pre-existed. The emotion DECISION is this Rule's own nested IfThenElse, not Python.
